text:
sam: Hey team — PR #7364 is ready for merge. Fixes alloc scheduler jitter; needs a 2nd approval and a quick smoke canary. Bench results + logs: https://bench.internal/runs/7364 :point_right:

morgan: Can you paste the perf deltas here? link is behind VPN for some of us.

sam: Sure — short summary: baseline -> post-change on our long-seq SLO workload (1000 tokens, mix of chats): P50 ~ unchanged, P95 +3%, P99 +11%, throughput -2%. Memory steady for steady-state, but warmup RSS increased ~120MB on 2xA100.

claire: Do you have the raw numbers? snippet is fine. Also any regression on microbatch horizon?

sam: pasted local bench snippet below:
```
benchmark: longseq-chat-v1
- baseline: P50=12ms P95=45ms P99=120ms tps=520 rss=7.1GB
- pr-7364: P50=12ms P95=46ms P99=133ms tps=510 rss=7.22GB
delta: P99 +13ms (+10.8%), throughput -2.0%, rss +120MB
```

raj: Memory delta seems small but that P99 bump worries me. Is this reproduced across canary regions?

sam: I ran canary in us-west2 via bench-bot — results landed: https://bench.internal/canary/7364 (summary below)

bench-bot: canary run 7364-us-west2 completed. status: FAIL (tail latency threshold exceeded)
```
canary summary: P50=13ms P95=47ms P99=140ms (threshold P99<=130ms)
error: p99_violation
logs: https://logs.internal/7364/canary-us-west2
```

morgan: Ok we should not merge until we understand root cause. @claire can you do a quick perf review? If it's caused by the scheduling heuristic in the allocator, we might revert or gate with runtime flag.

claire: I can take a look now. Quick eyeball: the change touched epoch alignment in alloc schedule, which can increase head-of-line wait for long sequences. If that's confirmed, we should add a config flag defaulting to old behavior and enable new heuristic via rollout.

sam: Sounds good. I can add a guard and a canary rollout plan. Also will add a test to repro longseq tail locally (script + seed).

raj: If timeline is tight, accept a temporary rollback. But let's try guard first. Who can approve after the fix? I can do a quick sign-off on the mem/alloc part once tests pass.

morgan: I'll give a formal review after the guard PR lands. For now holding merge.

claire: +1 to holding. I'll post inline comments in the PR and request changes on the heuristic behavior. Will try to finish in 60m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Thanks — I'll push a patch with a runtime flag branch + regression test in ~30m and update the canary plan. Ping me in #eng-oncall if we need to abort any running canaries.

morgan: thx. please include the smoke command you used locally so reviewers can reproduce quickly.

sam: adding command here:
```bash
# reproduce longseq smoke locally
python -m bench.run --profile longseq-chat-v1 --concurrency 8 --tokens 1000 --seed 42 --retries 3
```

claire: Nice. Once that's green and we add the flag I can approve. If bench-bot can re-run canary automatically after the patch lands that'd be ideal.

bench-bot: queued canary rerun once new patch is pushed (auto-trigger enabled).

sam: Will update PR and ping this thread when pushed. Thanks all. :clap:
